title: G1: Well-founded functional domains defined without presupposing SN

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (S1).** Construct, by recursion on simple types $\sigma$, a domain $\mathcal V_\sigma$ of (strictly monotone, inflationary) functionals together with an ordinal-valued measure $\mu_\sigma:\mathcal V_\sigma\to\mathrm{Ord}$, and prove the comparison used is **well-founded without any appeal to strong normalization**.

Base: $\mathcal V_o=(\mathbb N,<)$ (or an ordinal $\ge 1$).
Step: $\mathcal V_{\sigma\to\tau}=$ strictly monotone $f:\mathcal V_\sigma\to\mathcal V_\tau$.

**Why hard / load-bearing.** The pointwise order on $\mathbb N^{\mathbb N}$ is *not* well-founded, so one cannot simply compare functionals pointwise. The standard fix (Gandy/de Vrijer) is to compare only an attached ordinal weight $\mu$, or to restrict to eventually-affine / finitely-supported monotone functionals. A sloppy version silently re-imports SN. Deliverable: precise definition of $\mathcal V_\sigma,\mu_\sigma$ plus a proof that the relevant order is well-founded, citing only ordinal well-foundedness, never normalization.
